title: Randomized complexity of online labeling
formal: Determine, up to constant factors, the optimal amortized expected number of relabelings per insertion or deletion for randomized online list labeling with at most \(n\) live items and labels in \([2n]\), against an oblivious adversary. The target is one asymptotic rate \(f(n)\) with a matching upper bound and lower bound in the model below.
why: The problem measures the unavoidable movement needed to maintain a sorted array with spare capacity, a primitive used throughout ordered storage and indexing.

category_assignment.reason: Maintains ordered labels in a bounded array and charges relocations, a general representation primitive.

importance.reason: The problem measures the unavoidable movement needed to maintain a sorted array with spare capacity, a primitive used throughout ordered storage and indexing.

sentences: An ordered list is stored using a fixed range of numerical labels.
Insertions and deletions must preserve label order while keeping spare labels available.
The cost counts how many existing items receive a different label.
Randomization achieves nearly logarithmic expected amortized cost in the cited result.
The remaining task is to determine the optimal asymptotic rate for constant slack.

definitions: Fix a capacity \(n\ge2\) and start with an empty ordered list. An insertion specifies the rank at which a new distinct item enters the list; a deletion names a live item. The list never contains more than \(n\) items. After each update the algorithm assigns distinct labels from \(\{1,\ldots,2n\}\) to the live items, in strictly increasing list order. Cost is one for the update plus the number of surviving items whose labels change during it; assigning a label to the new item costs at most one additional unit. The input sequence is fixed independently of all random choices. Only relabelings are charged: local computation, rank search and auxiliary metadata are free, so this is a movement-cost model, not a word-RAM running-time target. An upper rate \(f\ge1\) means a uniform online algorithm and a constant \(C\) satisfy expected total cost at most \(C(n+M f(n))\) for every capacity and every finite valid sequence of \(M\) updates. For tightness, every algorithm and every rate \(g\) permitting such a bound must have \(g(n)=\Omega(f(n))\). Constants are independent of the sequence and capacity. The array has fixed constant slack; other label-universe regimes are outside this card.

context_blocks.text: The original catalog entry points to the randomized online-labeling question posed by Saks in 2017. This completed card fixes the constant-slack regime discussed in the researcher list.
The See-Saw Algorithm gives \(O(\log n\operatorname{polyloglog}n)\) amortized expected cost, while the cited randomized lower bound is \(\Omega(\log n)\). Its array size is \((1+\Theta(1))n\).

answer_criterion: Supply an explicit asymptotic rate and complete Lean-checked upper and matching lower bounds, up to absolute constant factors, for the expected amortized movement model specified here. A polylogarithmic-factor approximation or an analysis restricted to one algorithm family is insufficient.
